article_title: Including Learning Analytics in the Loop of Self-Paced Online Course Learning Design
citation: Hongxin Yan, Fuhua Lin & Kinshuk. (2021). Including Learning Analytics in the Loop of Self-Paced Online Course Learning Design. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education (2021) 31:878–895. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-020-00225-z
title: The Learning Design-Analytic (LDA) model: course learning design and learning analytics mutually support each other in self-paced online learning
description: The LDA model is a proposed model of learning design interacting with learning analytics, suggested mainly for STEM disciplines in self-paced online learning. In it, course learning design builds learning activities which generate learning data; learning analytics uses those data to mitigate SPOL learning barriers, and its results feed back to improve the design. The article states that 'course learning design that aims for learning success builds learning activities, which generate the learning data' and that analytics results 'can, in turn, empower the course learning design by facilitating a data-driven approach.'
requirements: Sufficient and meaningful data-collection points must be embedded in the course by designing certain learning activities, such as check-point activities like quizzes, posting, and reflecting
constraints: The model is suggested mainly for STEM disciplines in self-paced online learning in higher formal education
target_learners: adult learners in self-paced online higher education courses
target_learning_goals: learning success in STEM disciplines, including conceptual development, inquiry-based and problem-solving skills
examples: The COMP272 Data Structures and Algorithms course revision at Athabasca University follows the LDA model by planning a diagnostic test, a learner profile survey, and unit-level formative assessment.
key_sources: Hongxin Yan, Fuhua Lin & Kinshuk. (2021). Including Learning Analytics in the Loop of Self-Paced Online Course Learning Design. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education (2021) 31:878–895. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-020-00225-z

article_title: Effect of low-dose, high-frequency advanced life support training versus annual full-day training on simulation-based resuscitation performance: a randomized controlled trial.
citation: Moll Lisa, Riessen Reimer, Dahlmann Philipp, Häske David. (2026). Effect of low-dose, high-frequency advanced life support training versus annual full-day training on simulation-based resuscitation performance: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09717-3
title: Replace infrequent intensive refresher courses with regular short scenario-based sessions with feedback for maintaining resuscitation competence
description: The article recommends distributing resuscitation training as brief, recurring team scenarios rather than relying on annual intensive courses. Intervention participants trained "every 4 weeks, using a single CPR scenario in accordance with the ALS standard" in sessions of "about 10 to 15 min" ending with brief feedback. The authors argue short sessions "may represent a feasible alternative that integrates into the routine workflow" where time pressure limits extended training, and frame the superiority of the format via constructive alignment of objectives, activities and assessment.
requirements: Sessions must adhere to the ALS standard and conclude with brief feedback from qualified trainers
constraints: Benefits demonstrated only in a simulation-based, single-German-EMS-system, adult out-of-hospital context; translation to real cardiac arrest, in-hospital, pediatric or neonatal settings not established
target_learners: Emergency medical services professionals (paramedics and emergency medical technicians)
target_learning_goals: Maintain advanced life support competence and resuscitation team management skills over time
examples: The intervention group received CPR training every 4 weeks in 10–15 minute scenario sessions with brief feedback, while the control group received one ERC ALS course day
key_sources: Moll Lisa, Riessen Reimer, Dahlmann Philipp, Häske David. (2026). Effect of low-dose, high-frequency advanced life support training versus annual full-day training on simulation-based resuscitation performance: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09717-3

article_title: Effect of low-dose, high-frequency advanced life support training versus annual full-day training on simulation-based resuscitation performance: a randomized controlled trial.
citation: Moll Lisa, Riessen Reimer, Dahlmann Philipp, Häske David. (2026). Effect of low-dose, high-frequency advanced life support training versus annual full-day training on simulation-based resuscitation performance: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09717-3
title: Validated 29-item ALS resuscitation performance rating instrument with blinded expert and supplementary student rating
description: A self-developed rating instrument comprising four categories with 29 items covering technical and non-technical skills, each rated on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = poor, 5 = excellent). Items were refined from exploratory video analyses and reviewed by an interdisciplinary panel of six experts using a semi-structured consensus approach. Reliability was confirmed with "a Cronbach's alpha of 0.793 and an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.794 (95% confidence interval: 0.718-0.854)". Six blinded expert raters scored every video, and a supplementary blinded assessment by six student raters independently evaluated all 13 video scenarios.
requirements: Ratings are aggregated as mean scores per item from six independent, blinded raters; discrepancies are not resolved by consensus
constraints: Although validated, the instrument is not yet internationally established, and the score is a composite measure of guideline-adherent processes in a simulated setting that cannot be directly translated into patient outcomes
target_learners: Emergency medical services professionals (paramedics and emergency medical technicians)
target_learning_goals: Assess resuscitation management performance, including technical, non-technical and procedural domains
examples: The instrument was used to rate video-recorded standardized simulation scenarios at baseline and 12-month follow-up, with the team leader as the focus of evaluation
key_sources: Moll Lisa, Riessen Reimer, Dahlmann Philipp, Häske David. (2026). Effect of low-dose, high-frequency advanced life support training versus annual full-day training on simulation-based resuscitation performance: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-09717-3

article_title: Framing Metrics, Outcomes, and Assessment Overview in Leadership Programs.
citation: Hastings, L. J., and D. Rosch. 2025. "Framing Metrics, Outcomes, and Assessment Overview in Leadership Programs." New Directions for Student Leadership 2025, no. 187: 85–91. https://doi.org/10.1002/yd.70007
title: Leadership development advancements framework mapping research findings to outcome, assessment, and metric considerations
description: The article organizes advancements in leadership development research—complex context-influenced learners, leadership as dynamic process, longitudinal non-linear development, multi-level development, and early lifespan development—into a framework mapping each to outcome, assessment, and metric considerations. It states that "LD is longitudinal, non‐linear, multi‐level (both individual and team levels), happening earlier than we think, and largely influenced by context," challenging program design, metrics, outcomes, and assessment.
requirements: Assessment methods must be intentionally matched to the explicitly stated level of the program outcome
Longitudinal assessment should track an outcome over time with three or more waves of data and a sensible time metric
constraints: LE does not serve its intended purpose well via disconnected short‐term programs devoid of learner context and focused solely on leader development
target_learners: college and university students in leadership education programs
target_learning_goals: leadership learning and leader development across individual and collective levels
key_sources: Hastings, L. J., and D. Rosch. 2025. "Framing Metrics, Outcomes, and Assessment Overview in Leadership Programs." New Directions for Student Leadership 2025, no. 187: 85–91. https://doi.org/10.1002/yd.70007

article_title: Dear admission committee…: Which moves in application essays predict student master grades?
citation: de Boer, Van Rijnsoever, de Bresser. (2024). Dear admission committee…: Which moves in application essays predict student master grades? PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0304394
title: LDA-derived seven-move coding of application essays
description: A text-mining element in which Latent Dirichlet Allocation distills topics from application essays and aggregates them into moves, defined as "a functional unit of text, which has an identifiable purpose". Thirty topics were reduced to seven moves (master specific, research skills, prior education, societal impact, interest to learn, city and university, extracurricular); per-essay move probabilities (0–1) served as predictors of master grades. The approach replaces subjective essay ratings, which suffer poor interrater reliability, with probabilistic topic measures.
requirements: A corpus of application essays processed with stemming, lemmatization and stop-word removal, and a chosen number of topics (30 here) selected via topic-density criteria
constraints: The authors note the unstructured essay format and sheer volume of text make systematic assessment difficult, and essay-based admission may favor students from advantaged socio-economic backgrounds
target_learners: prospective master students in higher education
target_learning_goals: predicting study success for admission decisions
examples: Applied to 820 completed master files from four cohorts (2014–2017) at the Faculty of Geosciences, Utrecht University, across eleven English-taught two-year master programs
key_sources: de Boer, Van Rijnsoever, de Bresser. (2024). Dear admission committee…: Which moves in application essays predict student master grades? PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0304394

article_title: Helping babies breathe: assessing the effectiveness of simulation-based high-frequency recurring training in a community-based setting of Pakistan.
citation: Mubeen Kiran, Baig Marina, Abbas Sadia, Adnan Farzana, Lakhani Arusa, Bhamani Shireen Shehzad, Rehman Bushra, Shahid Shahnaz, Jan Rafat. (2021). Helping babies breathe: assessing the effectiveness of simulation-based high-frequency recurring training in a community-based setting of Pakistan. BMC Pediatrics. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12887-021-03014-2
title: Low Dose High Frequency (LDHF) capacity-building approach
description: LDHF is a capacity-building approach defined in the article as one that promotes maximal retention of clinical knowledge, skills, and attitudes through short, targeted in-service simulation-based learning activities, spaced over time, and reinforced with structured, ongoing practice sessions on the job. This study operationalized it as simulation-based high-frequency recurring HBB workshops with intermittent on-site supervision, adapted for community midwives who could not commute frequently for practice.
requirements: Short, targeted in-service simulation-based learning activities spaced over time
Structured ongoing on-the-job practice sessions or supervised support between sessions
constraints: The article notes applying LDHF in remote settings with community midwives was challenging and highly resource-intensive, motivating the centralized recurring-session adaptation
target_learners: In-service health workers such as community midwives in low-resource settings
target_learning_goals: Retention of clinical knowledge, skills, and attitudes for newborn resuscitation
examples: The study delivered all content in one day followed by two refresher sessions at two-month intervals, with random monthly supervision visits using the Neonatalie Simulator.
key_sources: Mubeen Kiran, Baig Marina, Abbas Sadia, Adnan Farzana, Lakhani Arusa, Bhamani Shireen Shehzad, Rehman Bushra, Shahid Shahnaz, Jan Rafat. (2021). Helping babies breathe: assessing the effectiveness of simulation-based high-frequency recurring training in a community-based setting of Pakistan. article_title: Simulation-based low-dose, high-frequency plus mobile mentoring versus traditional group-based trainings among health workers on day of birth care in Nigeria; a cluster randomized controlled trial.
citation: Ugwa Emmanuel, Kabue Mark, Otolorin Emmanuel, Yenokyan Gayane, Oniyire Adetiloye, Orji Bright, Okoli Ugo, Enne Joseph, Alobo Gabriel, Olisaekee Gladys, Oluwatobi Adebayo, Oduenyi Chioma, Aledare Adekunle, Onwe Boniface, Ishola Gbenga. (2020). Simulation-based low-dose, high-frequency plus mobile mentoring versus traditional group-based trainings among health workers on day of birth care in Nigeria; a cluster randomized controlled trial. BMC Health Services Research. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12913-020-05450-9
title: The LDHF/m-mentoring training approach: onsite, simulation-based, competency-focused low-dose high-frequency learning plus mobile mentoring
description: The LDHF/m-mentoring approach is a training model in which, per the article, "This approach primarily involves simulation education, onsite, more interactive, and team-oriented training". Its stated principles include competency-focused learning that concentrates on what providers "need to know", simulation- and case-based learning, appropriately spaced brief learning periods, team-focused facility-based training, ongoing practice and quality improvement, and peer coaching. Mobile mentoring reinforces gains through weekly SMS reminder messages and quiz questions and structured monthly mentoring calls from a master mentor.
requirements: Simulation aids such as anatomical models (MamaNatalie/NeoNatalie) for repeated deliberate practice
Peer Practice Coordinators to lead practice sessions and log practice
Mobile phone access so mentors can deliver reminder messages, quizzes, and monthly mentoring calls
constraints: Barriers reported qualitatively included different work schedules preventing group practice sessions and unavailability of equipment hindering translation into practice
The article notes operational challenges in ensuring mentors always had airtime for mobile mentoring
target_learners: Doctors, nurses and community health extension workers providing maternal and newborn day of birth care in low-resource facilities
target_learning_goals: BEmONC clinical skills competency including newborn resuscitation, active management of third stage of labour, PE/E and PPH management, and retention of those skills over 12 months
examples: In the trial, the intervention arm received two four-day onsite courses spaced one month apart, high-frequency simulation-based peer practice 2-3 times weekly between courses, and weekly SMS quizzes plus monthly half-hour PPC mentoring calls.
key_sources: Ugwa Emmanuel, Kabue Mark, Otolorin Emmanuel, Yenokyan Gayane, Oniyire Adetiloye, Orji Bright, Okoli Ugo, Enne Joseph, Alobo Gabriel, Olisaekee Gladys, Oluwatobi Adebayo, Oduenyi Chioma, Aledare Adekunle, Onwe Boniface, Ishola Gbenga. (2020). Simulation-based low-dose, high-frequency plus mobile mentoring versus traditional group-based trainings among health workers on day of birth care in Nigeria; a cluster randomized controlled trial. BMC Health Services Research. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12913-020-05450-9

article_title: From nuclei to neutron stars: simple binding energy computer modelling in the classroom (Part 1)
citation: Pastore A, Romero A M, Diget C, Rios A, Leech K and Stokoe P (2021). From nuclei to neutron stars: simple binding energy computer modelling in the classroom (Part 1). https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.06872
title: Liquid-drop (Bethe-Weizsäcker) mass formula: binding energy per particle as the sum of five terms
description: The article presents the Bethe-Weizsäcker liquid-drop mass formula, in which 'the model yields the binding energy per particle of an atomic nucleus as the sum of ﬁve terms' — volume, surface, Coulomb, asymmetry and pairing — with Table 1 coefficients aV = 15.8, aS = 18.3, aC = 0.714, aA = 23.2 and aP = 12.0 MeV. Each term is assigned a distinct physical meaning, from short-range nuclear attraction to proton Coulomb repulsion and pairing of nucleons.
requirements: Physical insight underpins the formula: one assumes that 'protons and neutrons form an incompressible droplet with a relatively sharp surface'.
constraints: The asymmetry and pairing terms 'require physical knowledge which is likely at an undergraduate level'.
The pairing term is a minor correction that 'may eventually be discarded to further simplify the model without loosing too much accuracy'.
target_learning_goals: understand the concept of binding energy
familiarise students with theoretical mathematical models
key_sources: Pastore A, Romero A M, Diget C, Rios A, Leech K and Stokoe P (2021). From nuclei to neutron stars: simple binding energy computer modelling in the classroom (Part 1). https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.06872

article_title: Uncovering shifts in the history of Physics education: a systematic, NLP-based, thematic analysis of articles from The Physics Teacher and Physics Education journals (1966-2019)
citation: Caramaschi, M. and Odden, T. O. B. (2024). Uncovering shifts in the history of Physics education: a systematic, NLP-based, thematic analysis of articles from The Physics Teacher and Physics Education journals (1966 - 2019). https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Uncovering+shifts+in+the+history+of+Physics+education
title: Latent Dirichlet Allocation as an unsupervised probabilistic topic model for uncovering thematic structure in large educational text corpora
description: Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) is a probabilistic generative model for topic modeling, originally introduced by Blei, Ng, and Jordan in 2003. It is an unsupervised method that discovers patterns in text without manual labeling, assuming each document is a blend of multiple topics characterized by co-occurring word distributions. The article uses LDA within a "bag of words" approach to calculate topic prevalence across decades of physics teaching articles, integrating it with qualitative thematic interpretation to label and track 20 topics over time.
requirements: Researchers must specify the number of topics, topic overlap, and text preprocessing choices before running the model
Topics output as weighted word lists require researcher interpretation to assign meaning
constraints: Results may vary slightly between runs because the model is probabilistic and randomly initialized, requiring careful validation
target_learning_goals: large-scale thematic review and trend analysis of educational literature
examples: The article applied LDA to 13,648 articles from The Physics Teacher and Physics Education, testing 15 to 22 topic configurations and validating with coherence scores
key_sources: Caramaschi, M. and Odden, T. O. B. (2024). Uncovering shifts in the history of Physics education: a systematic, NLP-based, thematic analysis of articles from The Physics Teacher and Physics Education journals (1966 - 2019). https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Uncovering+shifts+in+the+history+of+Physics+education

article_title: Simulation-based low-dose, high-frequency plus mobile mentoring versus traditional group-based training approaches on day of birth care among maternal and newborn healthcare providers in Ebonyi and Kogi States, Nigeria; a randomized controlled trial.
citation: Ugwa Emmanuel, Otolorin Emmanuel, Kabue Mark, Ishola Gbenga, Evans Cherrie, Oniyire Adetiloye, Olisaekee Gladys, Onwe Boniface, LeFevre Amnesty E, Bluestone Julia, Orji Bright, Yenokyan Gayane, Okoli Ugo. (2018). Simulation-based low-dose, high-frequency plus mobile mentoring versus traditional group-based training approaches on day of birth care among maternal and newborn healthcare providers in Ebonyi and Kogi States, Nigeria; a randomized controlled trial. BMC Health Services Research. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12913-018-3405-2
title: The LDHF approach: short, structured, onsite, interactive learning activities spaced over time to optimize learning
description: The article defines the low-dose, high-frequency (LDHF) approach as an in-service learning model that delivers "information based on local needs during short, structured, onsite, interactive learning activities that involve the entire team and are spaced over time to optimize learning." It also involves brief ongoing onsite activities such as skills practice, team drills, games, and quality improvement activities to sustain learning and support clinical decision-making. The trial is designed to test LDHF plus mobile mentoring against traditional offsite group training.
requirements: Training must be onsite at the health facility and involve the entire team of providers
constraints: The article notes the evidence base from low- and middle-income countries is limited, with severe lack of quality data from LMICs
target_learners: Doctors, nurses, midwives and community health extension workers providing maternal and newborn care
target_learning_goals: Clinical knowledge and skills in day of birth care (BEmONC competencies)
examples: MCSP is applying the approach in Ebonyi and Kogi States, Nigeria to build evidence supporting the shift from offsite group-based training to LDHF

title: Seven enumerated design characteristics of the LDHF training approach
description: The article enumerates the principles of the LDHF approach: competency-focused learning activities that concentrate on what providers "need to know"; simulation- and case-based learning focused on skills practice, problem-solving and role-play; appropriately spaced brief periods of learning delivered in 1 day or over several days; team-focused training; facility-based training that decreases absenteeism and improves teamwork; ongoing practice and quality improvement activities; and facility-based peer staff coaching others as they practice. Dosing and frequency depend on topic, extent of the learning gap, and learner characteristics.
requirements: Peer practice coordinators must coach others as they practice after learning to increase compliance
constraints: Dosing and frequency depend on topic, extent of the learning gap, and learner characteristics
target_learners: In-service maternal and newborn healthcare provider teams at health facilities
target_learning_goals: Clinical competency in day of birth care and transfer of learning to clinical practice
examples: The trial's LDHF arm operationalizes these characteristics: two 4-day onsite courses one month apart, high-frequency simulation practice 2-3 times weekly, PPC coaching, and SMS mentoring

title: Simulation-based LDHF/m-Mentoring training intervention: two 4-day onsite courses, weekly simulation practice, SMS quizzes, and monthly mentor calls
description: The intervention arm consists of two 4-day "low-dose" onsite BEmONC training courses repeated after 1 month, with lecture time reduced and hands-on practice increased. Between courses, providers practice via "high-frequency simulation-based practices of 2-3 times weekly" logged by Peer Practice Coordinators. Mobile mentoring consists of weekly SMS reminder messages and quiz questions, plus structured monthly half-hour mentoring calls from a trainer/master mentor for PPCs. MamaNatalie/NeoNatalie manikins are used for simulation.

target_learning_goals: BEmONC knowledge and skills at 80% or higher competence level
examples: At the end of each four-day training participants undergo immediate post-training MCQ and OSCE assessment with a 80% competence threshold

article_title: Thematic Analysis of 18 Years of PERC Proceedings using Natural Language Processing
citation: Tor Ole B. Odden, Alessandro Marin, and Marcos D. Caballero. (2018). Thematic Analysis of 18 Years of PERC Proceedings using Natural Language Processing. https://github.com/uio-ccse/PERC_TopicModel
title: Latent Dirichlet Allocation as a generative probabilistic topic model
description: Latent Dirichlet Allocation is "a generative probabilistic modeling technique that tries to extract the latent or hidden themes from a set of texts or documents". It assumes documents are mixtures of latent topics, each topic a weighted distribution over words, and reverse-engineers topic-word and document-topic distributions from word co-occurrence using a bag-of-words simplification. The article presents LDA as epistemologically similar to simplified toy models in physics, requiring user-specified K and α parameters and multiple levels of validation.
requirements: The user must specify the number of topics (K) and the topic-mixture parameter α in advance
Validation via coherence scores and face-validity checks, since unsupervised methods have no ground truth
constraints: The model disregards word order (bag of words)
It assumes every document is a mixture of several topics
Random initialization means topics change from run to run across models trained with identical parameters
target_learners: education researchers analyzing a research literature corpus
target_learning_goals: characterizing themes and their evolution in an educational research literature
examples: An LDA model trained on roughly 9000 Huffington Post headlines reproduced three pre-established human-coded themes (sports, religion, technology) when given K = 3 topics
key_sources: Tor Ole B. Odden, Alessandro Marin, and Marcos D. Caballero. (2018). Thematic Analysis of 18 Years of PERC Proceedings using Natural Language Processing. https://github.com/uio-ccse/PERC_TopicModel

article_title: Trends, Impact, and Thematic Evolution of Physics Education: A Bibliometric and Topic Modelling Analysis of Six Decades of Publications
citation: Purwoko Haryadi Santoso, Nurlina and Mutmainna. (2026). Trends, Impact, and Thematic Evolution of Physics Education: A Bibliometric and Topic Modelling Analysis of Six Decades of Publications. https://github.com/santosoph/PED-Bibliometric
title: Five-topic LDA taxonomy of Physics Education research themes
description: The study uses latent Dirichlet allocation on article abstracts to map the journal's intellectual structure. LDA "assumes that each document is characterized by a mixture of topics and that each topic is represented by a probability distribution over words", and model selection combined statistical fit, coherence, and interpretability. The resulting five topics are force and motion experiments (FME), energy and light experiments (ELE), laboratory-based learning (LBL), conceptual understanding (CU), and physics teacher education (PTE), with topic labels assigned through researcher interpretation rather than directly by the algorithm.
requirements: Abstracts with complete metadata for all analyzed publications, preprocessed via stop-word removal, lemmatization, and sparsity thresholding at 0.99
constraints: Topic labels were concluded through researcher interpretation rather than directly by the algorithm; results are influenced by preprocessing decisions, topic-number selection, and LDA assumptions
target_learning_goals: mapping the thematic structure and evolution of physics education research
examples: The five-topic solution (K = 5) was selected after comparing LDA models with varying topic numbers using fit indices, topic coherence, and semantic interpretability
key_sources: Purwoko Haryadi Santoso, Nurlina and Mutmainna. (2026). Trends, Impact, and Thematic Evolution of Physics Education: A Bibliometric and Topic Modelling Analysis of Six Decades of Publications. https://github.com/santosoph/PED-Bibliometric
